findings.title: Secret in a client-visible flag value: payment_config
findings.subject: payment_config

explanation.title: Secret in a client-visible flag value: payment_config
explanation.what_happened: The flag payment_config serves a credential to every visitor.
explanation.why_it_matters: Flag values in a client-side environment are public; a key stored there is already exposed.
explanation.business_impact: Someone could use the credential to act as your service.
explanation.fix_summary: Rotate the credential, then move it to server-side configuration or mark the flag server-side only.

findings.subject: admins

explanation.title: Forging role=admin unlocks admin_panel (segment "admins")
explanation.what_happened: Anyone can claim user attributes such as role=admin from the browser and Flagsmith accepts them, unlocking admin_panel.
explanation.why_it_matters: The environment lets client-side code set traits, so targeting rules based on traits are not a security boundary.
explanation.business_impact: Paid or privileged features can be used without paying or being authorised.
explanation.fix_summary: Turn off client-side traits for this environment, or move the decision to your server.

evidence.note: Flagsmith's engine serves on instead of off for flag "admin_panel" to an identity with trait/identifier role="admin" (segment "admins"; forgeable: yes).

findings.subject: pricing_page

explanation.why_it_matters: Experiment results can be manipulated by anyone who knows the public key.
explanation.business_impact: Decisions based on the experiment may be wrong.
explanation.fix_summary: Keep experiment identifiers server-side and review the results for contamination.

explanation.what_happened: The flag payment_config is visible to browsers but looks server-only.
explanation.why_it_matters: Only flags marked server-side only are kept out of client responses.
explanation.business_impact: Server configuration is readable by anyone.
explanation.fix_summary: Mark the flag as server-side only.

findings.title: Re-rolling the identifier unlocks early_access_ai (≈9% rollout, ~11 tries)
findings.subject: early_access_ai

explanation.title: Re-rolling the identifier unlocks early_access_ai (≈9% rollout, ~11 tries)
explanation.what_happened: A visitor can keep choosing new identifiers until they land in the rollout group for early_access_ai.
explanation.why_it_matters: Percentage rollouts are decided by the identifier, which the client controls.
explanation.business_impact: Gated or early-access features can be reached on demand, and rollout numbers become unreliable.
explanation.fix_summary: Do not use percentage rollouts as access control; derive identifiers on the server.

evidence.note: Flagsmith's engine serves on instead of off for flag "early_access_ai" to an identity with trait/identifier identifier="gc-probe-map-9" (segment "canary_10"; forgeable: yes).

findings.title: Production: "Allow client SDKs to set user traits" is ON
findings.subject: allow_client_traits

explanation.title: Production: "Allow client SDKs to set user traits" is ON
explanation.what_happened: The environment allow_client_traits allows client-side traits.
explanation.why_it_matters: Anyone with the public key can send traits that change flag results.
explanation.fix_summary: Disable client traits after confirming no app code needs them.

evidence.note: Environment "Production": dashboard setting "Allow client SDKs to set user traits" is ON (allow_client_traits). Anyone holding the public client key can set their own traits, so any segment keyed on a trait can be forged. Turn this setting off for every environment that uses segments for access control.

explanation.title: Production: "Hide sensitive data" is OFF
explanation.what_happened: The environment hide_sensitive_data does not hide sensitive data.
explanation.why_it_matters: Sensitive flag data is returned to client-side requests.
explanation.business_impact: Secrets and internal details reach browsers.
explanation.fix_summary: Enable the hide sensitive data setting.

evidence.note: Environment "Production": dashboard setting "Hide sensitive data" is OFF (hide_sensitive_data). Sensitive data is not hidden in this environment. Turn this setting on.
